title: THE WHALE THAT SWALLOWED THE EXIT
deck: The living wall of a collapsing cosmos has closed the only door out, and every cut makes the clock shorter. Illuminara cannot outargue a wound, so she asks what a touch has to feel like to be a touch, and what the wall will let her do with one.
shape: Seven scenes across thirty-seven hours: a cut that costs three, a pilots' word, a crossing that fails at four hundred metres, an offer the wall refuses and then accepts, a council that gives the call away, a pause nobody breaks, and a far shore where the lamps answer a wave.

scenes.title: The Cut That Cost Three Hours
paragraphs: *Harbor Nine, the Rim of the Calyx · thirty-seven hours to collapse*
The Brannock went into the Seam at slack water, which was when every engineer in the Calyx said it should, and for eleven seconds Illuminara thought they might be right.

She stood on the harbor gantry beside Dunya Quor, the convoy dispatcher, and watched six hundred metres of cutting arm unfold from the freighter's nose. Ahead lay the Seam, a wet black doorway forty kilometres across in the living wall that held the Calyx apart from the outer dark. The pilots called the wall Uluun, after the sound the old buoys made when it moved. The harbor children called it the whale, because it had swallowed the one exit the way a whale takes a boat, and because every child had been told that whales give things back. Behind the harbor the Calyx was folding in on its own weight, and four hundred cities and six billion people waited for one way out.

Then the wall flinched. It flinched before the arms touched anything, a long shudder that ran up the doorframe and drew the edges inward, and the Brannock's cutters closed on their own reflections. On the harbor board the clock jumped. 37:00 became 34:12.

**Hale Corvane**  
Bigger cutters, closer together. We budgeted three hours for the cost of a door that size, and we are through before it understands what is happening.

**Illuminara**  
It understood in the first second. It flinched a heartbeat before the arms touched it. Not at the cut. Before.

**Dunya**  
That's the hum. Our cutters run at forty cycles, and you feel it in the deck plates before the arms drop. We cut at slack, when the tissue is loosest.

**Illuminara**  
Then it has felt that hum a great many times before today.
Corvane turned from the rail, delegate for Tamsin Deep and its four million. *He is not a cruel man,* she thought. *I am the first person all week to ask him to spend his clock on a question.*

**Hale Corvane**  
You are proposing we spare the creature's feelings with thirty-four hours left.

**Illuminara**  
I'm proposing we stop paying three hours every time we ask it to open. I could hold one corner of that doorframe in my hands for the length of a convoy. It would be the same harpoon, only more polite.
Nobody on the gantry doubted that she could. That was what made it a hard thing to say.

**Dunya**  
What do you want, then?

**Illuminara**  
Every record of the wall being hurt. And anyone who has ever crossed it without cutting.
Where the cutters had been, a long ripple was travelling away along the wall at the pace of a walking man. Illuminara watched it go and did not yet know what she was looking at.

scenes.title: Slack
paragraphs: *The pilots' galley, Harbor Nine · thirty-four hours*

The scar survey covered the galley table: three thousand and forty-one pale marks on a chart of the wall, each one a place where something had once been cut into Uluun and left. Ysa Quor, Dunya's mother, had flown tide-ferries for sixty years and held opinions about every vessel in the harbor, including this table.

**Ysa**  
Prospectors' cuts, mostly. Before the Calyx had a name. Nobody has cut that wall in my lifetime until this week.

**Illuminara**  
They all sit on the same band of the wave. Slack, under a hum like the Brannock's. In every way it can feel, we are exactly like them.
She turned the chart under the lamp. Three thousand and thirty dots, eleven that did not belong, and three smooth blanks on the outer face where the probes had come back with no echo at all.

**Illuminara**  
Those three aren't scars. They're places that stopped answering. Who did that?

**Ysa**  
Older than the harbor. Whatever did it came from outside.
She set the blanks aside. The eleven had no scar tissue and no dead margin: something had gone through the wall and it had closed behind the thing clean.

**Illuminara**  
Where do the eleven sit on the wave?

**Dunya**  
The crest. Every one of them.

**Ysa**  
Drift-boats.
The old woman set her mug down.

**Ysa**  
You waited for the crest, killed your engines and let it carry you. My great-grandmother did it with eight aboard and one lantern. Nobody could do it with a city.

**Illuminara**  
What did you do aboard while it carried you?

**Ysa**  
Hummed. Low, so you couldn't say it was a song. Boat-hum.

**Illuminara**  
Why?

**Ysa**  
So whatever's carrying you knows there's somebody in the hull. Nobody ever asked it whether that helped.
Eleven clean scars and an old woman's habit were not a theory. *A guess with a hull attached,* Illuminara thought. *Test it small, and let everyone aboard be someone who chose to be there.*

**Dunya**  
There's a crest in three hours.

**Ysa**  
Then you'll want the Lark. She's slow and ugly and has the best-kept hull in the harbor. And I'm coming. I have done this, girl. You haven't.

scenes.title: The Lark at Crest
paragraphs: *The Lark, foredeck, the mouth of the Seam · thirty-one hours*

Four hundred volunteers rode the Lark, because no one had been willing to ask for fewer. Dunya cut the main drive at the lip of the Seam and kept only the attitude thrusters, because a ship with none is a log.

The crest came as a rising of the floor of the world. The doorframe did not tear open. It unfolded, slowly, like a hand, and the Lark slid in on the long swell as if the wall had been waiting to hold her. Below decks Ysa began to hum, so low it could not be called a song, and the sound went hull by hull until the bulkheads shook gently with it.
For four hundred metres the Lark was carried.
Then the swell began to set her toward the edge of the doorframe.

**Dunya**  
Thirty metres to the wall on the port side. I need the thrusters.

**Illuminara**  
Have you anything else?

**Dunya**  
No.
There was nothing else. The thrusters fired, a tiny forty-cycle hum, and the swell stopped being a hand.

It did not crush her. It threw her out. The spine cracked with a single dry sound, and Illuminara dropped onto the main beam and took the weight of a ship. She held it for ninety seconds while the crew went over the side into lifeboats. Then she let the Lark go, and the ship folded in on itself like paper.
Eleven people had broken bones. No one was dead. The harbor clock took forty more minutes, and Hale Corvane stood under it with his arms folded.

**Hale Corvane**  
Three hours for a cut that taught us nothing. Forty minutes for a ship that taught you two things.

**Hale Corvane**  
Then I want the rest of the answer. Not before.

**Dunya**  
I fired the thrusters.

**Illuminara**  
You had thirty metres and nothing else. I never told you what you'd hit. That is mine to carry, not yours.
In the lifeboat Ysa sat with a bandaged wrist, still humming at nobody.

**Ysa**  
It carried us while we hummed.

**Illuminara**  
It did. It carried us four hundred metres while we were quiet, and it threw us the instant we fired. That's two things to learn, not one: when to touch it, and what the touch has to sound like.

scenes.title: The Ocean
paragraphs: *Inside Uluun, through the window · twenty-seven hours, slack water*
She settled the terms first, because a visit that cannot be ended is not a visit.

**Illuminara**  
If it flinches, I leave. Not when I've understood it. When it flinches. Then I stay out until it has had the better part of an hour to decide, and I go back only to offer again, never to ask why.

**Dunya**  
Three taps on your hand, and your name. If you haven't answered by the quarter hour I'm coming in with a mallet.
She opened the window a hand's width and left its door where Dunya's three taps could find her. Her body stayed on the harbor deck. The rest of her went down into weight.

It was not water and it was not dark. It was pressure, huge and slow, a mind that did not speak but leaned, something vast that surfaced and took a door into itself and kept it. At slack the whole ocean ached around a single cold line, a forty-cycle hum running through its body like a thread through cloth, and beside the line were three patches of nothing, where it had stopped hearing. She did not reach for them. They were not hers to open. She felt one want, and it was not hers to meet by force: to be touched by something that took nothing away.

The ocean flinched at her coming. She did not argue. She went out in the same breath, to the deck and Dunya's three taps, and sat for fifty minutes with her hands open on her knees. The first no was an answer, and she let it stand as one.

The second offer began when the swell turned toward crest. She went in smaller than before, and brought Ysa's hum alone, once, before any hull carried it. Twenty-five cycles, well under the cutters' forty. Low, unhurried, with nothing underneath it.

The ocean did not flinch. It leaned, not toward her but toward the hum. When she let the hum break, the lean went slack, and the whole swell began to slide toward its rim, as water runs to the edge of a tilted tray. It wanted a middle, and nothing was marking one. So she asked the only question she had. She set the hum low and to one side, and the lean went there. She set it at the centre of the span, and the lean went there. Where the hum was, the swell went.

Then she understood the Lark. Ysa's hum had ridden inside the thing being carried, and when the hull wandered, the middle wandered with it. A hum set ahead of the hulls, on the centreline, would be a middle that did not move. It was a handle, and it was the wall's to let go of at any moment.
The swell, climbing toward its crest, lingered a few seconds on the way.
*A maybe,* she thought. *Not a promise. It doesn't owe me a promise.*
She had been the largest thing in most rooms of her life. Here the thing holding her had no reason to. It felt like being allowed.
Three taps. Then her name. She came out.

scenes.title: Dark Cities
paragraphs: *Council hall, Harbor Nine · twenty-five hours*

She laid it out in four minutes. Three crests were left. The cities would cross in three pulses, engines cold, lamps out, every hull humming, behind a dead-engined skiff, the pacer, that would run ahead on the centreline humming Ysa's twenty-five cycles. Uluun could stop any pulse by stalling its swell, and no one would fire a drive.

**Hale Corvane**  
Six billion people on a swell we have put a handle on, in the dark, at the pleasure of a creature that threw a ship across the harbor yesterday. The Lark hummed too, Illuminara. What makes your skiff different?

**Illuminara**  
The Lark carried her hum inside her, so it went where she drifted. The pacer's hum goes ahead of us, on the centreline, so the swell has a middle that doesn't move.

**Hale Corvane**  
And if it stops?

**Illuminara**  
Then you wait.

**Hale Corvane**  
And if the clock runs out while we wait?

**Illuminara**  
Then some of us don't get out. I won't buy them with a second harpoon, Delegate.

**Hale Corvane**  
Then the call isn't yours. When it stops, a pilot on the lead deck decides when we wait and when we run for the boats. I won't have the one person who could lift a city decide it's allowed to drop. Dunya.

**Illuminara**  
Agreed. Dunya's call, and I'll abide by it.
A dockhand at the back stood up with a child's mitten folded in his fist. His name was Marro Tell.

**Marro Tell**  
I don't like it, and I don't like that nobody asked those of us who'll sit in the dark with children. I've got three. I'm not humming at a wall.

**Illuminara**  
You shouldn't have to. There is a second way, the rim drift: boats along the wall's edge on the first crest, no hum, thirty hours to the far shore, while the cities cross in six hours. I'll chart it tonight with a pilot of your choosing, and nobody will call it the cowards' road.

**Marro Tell**  
They'll call it that.

**Dunya**  
Then they'll say it to my face. I'll have the call, and I'll see your boats from the lead deck.
Corvane was still looking at the chart. What he asked next cost him something to say.

**Hale Corvane**  
Tamsin Deep takes the last pulse. If it is going to stop on anyone, let it stop on four million of mine, after they have watched the first two get through.

**Illuminara**  
That's the hardest place in the line. Why choose it?

**Hale Corvane**  
Because I would rather be the last to believe you than the first to be wrong.

scenes.title: The First Pulse
paragraphs: *The Seam, the deck of Veyra Hold, lamps out · twenty-three hours*

At the crest the doorframe opened as it had for the Lark, and a hundred and thirty-three cities went into it with their engines cold. The pacer ran ahead on the centreline, six pilots in a dead skiff humming Ysa's twenty-five cycles. Illuminara stood on the lead deck in her ordinary body, with Ysa's chair beside her and Dunya at the rail. Within a minute the hum was two billion people with their palms on bulkheads.
The swell took them up like breath. At the eighth minute it began to set toward the port edge. The pacer had drifted a hull-length off the line, and the swell had gone with it.

**Dunya**  
Pacer, back to the middle. Everyone else keep your palms down.

Dunya never reached for a thruster. The skiff's pilots shifted their note, and the swell came back to them as a sleeper turns toward a warm back. Far to port, along the rim, a string of small lights drifted silent on the same crest. Marro Tell's boats. Nobody on them hummed.
At the thirty-first minute the swell stopped.

It did not clamp. It did not throw. The whole wave simply held, a hundred and thirty-three cities hanging in living tissue and no sound anywhere but the hum. Somewhere far down its body an old cut had passed under the tide and woken. Over the open channel, from the dark deck of Tamsin Deep, came Hale Corvane's voice.

**Hale Corvane**  
Veyra Hold, the lamps say it has stopped. You have the call, pilot.

**Dunya**  
We could fire the drives. Nine minutes of crest left.

**Ysa**  
Say why not. I want to hear it said out loud.

**Illuminara**  
Because it is the only thing in this whole crossing that gets to say stop. If it can't, we were never carried. We broke a door with better manners.

**Dunya**  
Then I'm calling a wait. Pacer, keep humming. Everyone else, palms down.

It was the hardest thing Illuminara did that day, and it looked like nothing. She stood on a dark deck with a power that could have lifted the city on its back, and she did not use it, and the one who held the call called it for her.

For eleven minutes the wave did not move. Then it moved, and the crest, which should have been gone at the fortieth minute, stayed. It lingered nearly an hour. The whale was giving back the time it had taken.
The second pulse stopped for four minutes, and nobody touched a drive. The third, with Tamsin Deep at its head, did not stop at all.

scenes.title: What the Wave Carried
paragraphs: *The far side, the new dark · thirty hours after the first pulse*

There were no stars. Six billion people stood on the decks of four hundred cities and looked back at the place where their sky had been. The Calyx had gone out hours ago, the way a house does when a door shuts on it.
Ysa sat on a bench with her wrist in a sling. The rim boats had come in on the thirtieth hour, every one of them, and Marro Tell came up the gangway with his three children and did not look pleased.

**Marro Tell**  
I've nothing kind to say about the dark. But mine are alive, and nobody hummed at anybody who didn't want to. Next time you ask us first.

**Illuminara**  
You're right. We drew the cities first and the boats second. The next plan begins with you.
Behind the cities lay Uluun's scar, a ridge forty kilometres long, pale and raw. Dunya came along the deck with a roster of ten thousand volunteers for the scar crews, Corvane's name first.

**Dunya**  
We'll walk with it. Not settle. Walk. Generations of it.

**Ysa**  
And no stars.

**Illuminara**  
No stars. But it carried you, and it let the scar stay open to be tended.
Along the outer face the three blanks still held no echo. Ysa looked at them a long time and said nothing, and Illuminara left them to be what they were.

The wave turned. Uluun was leaving, away from the closing dark, toward a route only it had chosen, the cities strung out behind it. As the swell passed under each one, someone aboard lit a single lamp in time with it. One, and then another, a greeting made the slow way.

**Ysa**  
It isn't answering.

**Illuminara**  
It doesn't owe us an answer.

**Ysa**  
Then why is it slowing down?
And it was, by a hair, enough for the lamps at the back of the line to catch up.

critic_line: Illuminara learns that a wounded living wall flinches before the blade, offers it a refusable hum, hands the call to the pilot who may wait, and six billion people cross a collapsing cosmos behind a dead-engined skiff while the wall keeps its scar and its own course.

shared_strengths: Strong premise (the wall as a living creature that must consent), humane ethic of asking rather than cutting, and dialogue-heavy structure suit these readers. Dense invented jargon, many named characters and abrupt compressed plot turns (the wave mechanics, the pulses) may blunt emotional pull and clarity.

The vivid living-wall premise, escalating tests, substantial dialogue, and humane emphasis on consent create strong narrative and emotional momentum. Illuminara’s restraint becomes gripping action rather than abstraction, and the final lamp sequence is memorable. Dense numerical exposition and occasional overt moral signaling may slightly reduce immersion for some readers.
shared_reservations: Twenty-five cycles, well under the cutters' forty. Low, unhurried, with nothing underneath it.
Three thousand and thirty dots, eleven that did not belong, and three smooth blanks on the outer face where the probes had come back with no echo at all.

translation_sl.title: KIT, KI JE POGOLTNIL IZHOD
translation_sl.deck: Živi zid sesedajočega se kozmosa je zaprl edina vrata ven in vsak rez skrajša preostali čas. Illuminara rane ne more premagati z argumentom, zato vpraša, kakšen mora biti dotik, da se čuti kot dotik, in kaj ji bo zid dovolil storiti z njim.
translation_sl.shape: Sedem prizorov v sedemintridesetih urah: rez, ki stane tri ure; beseda pilotov; prečkanje, ki spodleti po štiristo metrih; ponudba, ki jo zid najprej zavrne, nato sprejme; svet, ki preda odločitev; premor, ki ga nihče ne prekrši; in oddaljena obala, kjer luči odgovorijo valu.

scenes.title: Rez, ki je stal tri ure
paragraphs: *Harbor Nine, rob Calyxa · sedemintrideset ur do sesutja*
Brannock je vstopil v Seam ob mirni vodi, ko bi po besedah vseh inženirjev v Calyxu moral, in enajst sekund je Illuminara mislila, da imajo morda prav.

Stala je na pristaniškem mostovžu ob Dunyi Quor, dispečerki konvoja, in opazovala, kako se s premca tovorne ladje razpira šeststo metrov dolga rezalna roka. Pred njima je ležal Seam, mokra črna vrata, široka štirideset kilometrov, v živem zidu, ki je Calyx ločeval od zunanje teme. Piloti so zidu rekli Uluun, po zvoku starih boj, kadar se je premaknil. Pristaniški otroci so mu rekli kit, ker je pogoltnil edini izhod, kakor kit pogoltne čoln, in ker so vsakemu otroku povedali, da kiti stvari vrnejo. Za pristaniščem se je Calyx gubal pod lastno težo, štiristo mest in šest milijard ljudi pa je čakalo na eno samo pot ven.

Nato je zid trznil. Trznil je, preden so se roke česarkoli dotaknile, z dolgim drgetom, ki je stekel navzgor po vratnem okviru in potegnil robove navznoter, Brannockovi rezalniki pa so se zaprli okoli lastnih odsevov. Na pristaniški tabli je ura preskočila. 37:00 je postalo 34:12.

**Hale Corvane**  
Večji rezalniki, tesneje skupaj. Tri ure smo namenili ceni tako velikih vrat in skoznje bomo, še preden zid razume, kaj se dogaja.

**Illuminara**  
Razumel je v prvi sekundi. Trznil je za utrip srca, preden so se ga roke dotaknile. Ne ob rezu. Pred njim.

**Dunya**  
To je brnenje. Naši rezalniki delujejo pri štiridesetih ciklih in čutiš jih v krovnih ploščah, preden se roke spustijo. Režemo ob mirni vodi, ko je tkivo najbolj ohlapno.

**Illuminara**  
Potem je to brnenje pred današnjim dnem občutil že zelo velikokrat.
Corvane se je obrnil od ograje, delegat za Tamsin Deep in njegove štiri milijone. *Ni krut človek,* je pomislila. *Jaz sem prva oseba ves teden, ki ga prosi, naj del svojega časa nameni vprašanju.*

**Hale Corvane**  
Predlagaš, naj pri štiriintridesetih preostalih urah varujemo čustva tega bitja.

**Illuminara**  
Predlagam, da nehamo plačevati tri ure vsakič, ko ga prosimo, naj se odpre. En vogal tega vratnega okvira bi lahko v rokah držala ves čas prehoda konvoja. To bi bila ista harpuna, le vljudnejša.
Nihče na mostovžu ni dvomil, da bi to zmogla. Prav zato je bilo to težko reči.

**Dunya**  
Kaj torej želiš?

**Illuminara**  
Vse zapise o tem, kako je bil zid ranjen. In kogarkoli, ki ga je kdaj prečkal brez rezanja.
Od mesta, kjer so bili rezalniki, je vzdolž zidu s hitrostjo hodečega človeka potovalo dolgo valovanje. Illuminara ga je opazovala in še ni vedela, kaj gleda.

scenes.title: Mirna voda
paragraphs: *Pilotska kuhinja, Harbor Nine · štiriintrideset ur*

Pregled brazgotin je prekrival kuhinjsko mizo: tri tisoč enainštirideset bledih znamenj na zemljevidu zidu, vsako na kraju, kjer je bilo nekoč nekaj zarezano v Uluun in zapuščeno. Ysa Quor, Dunyina mati, je šestdeset let upravljala plimske trajekte in imela mnenje o vsakem plovilu v pristanišču, tudi o tej mizi.

**Ysa**  
Večinoma rezi iskalcev. Še preden je Calyx imel ime. V mojem življenju do tega tedna nihče ni rezal tega zidu.

**Illuminara**  
Vsi ležijo na istem pasu vala. Ob mirni vodi, pod brnenjem, kakršno ima Brannock. Na vsak način, ki ga lahko občuti, smo natanko takšni kot oni.
Zemljevid je obrnila pod svetilko. Tri tisoč trideset pik, enajst takih, ki tja niso sodile, in tri gladke praznine na zunanji strani, kjer so se sonde vrnile brez kakršnegakoli odmeva.

**Illuminara**  
Te tri niso brazgotine. To so mesta, ki so nehala odgovarjati. Kdo je to storil?

**Ysa**  
Starejše so od pristanišča. Karkoli je to storilo, je prišlo od zunaj.
Praznine je odložila na stran. Enajst znamenj ni imelo brazgotinskega tkiva niti odmrlega roba: nekaj je šlo skozi zid, ta pa se je za njim čisto zaprl.

**Illuminara**  
Kje na valu leži teh enajst?

**Dunya**  
Na vrhu. Vseh enajst.

**Ysa**  
Plovne barke.
Starka je odložila skodelico.

**Ysa**  
Počakal si na vrh, ugasnil motorje in pustil, da te odnese. Moja prababica je to storila z osmimi ljudmi na krovu in eno svetilko. Z mestom tega ne bi mogel nihče.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj ste počeli na krovu, medtem ko vas je nosil?

**Ysa**  
Brneli smo. Nizko, da temu nisi mogel reči pesem. Brnenje čolna.

**Illuminara**  
Zakaj?

**Ysa**  
Da tisto, kar te nosi, ve, da je nekdo v trupu. Nihče ga ni nikoli vprašal, ali je to pomagalo.

Enajst čistih brazgotin in navada stare ženske niso bili teorija. *Ugibanje s pritrjenim trupom,* je pomislila Illuminara. *Preizkusi ga v majhnem in naj bo vsak na krovu nekdo, ki se je odločil biti tam.*

**Dunya**  
Čez tri ure bo vrh.

**Ysa**  
Potem boš hotela Lark. Počasna je in grda ter ima najbolje ohranjen trup v pristanišču. In jaz grem zraven. Jaz sem to že naredila, dekle. Ti nisi.

scenes.title: Lark na vrhu
paragraphs: *Lark, premčna paluba, ustje Seama · enaintrideset ur*

Štiristo prostovoljcev je plulo na Lark, ker nihče ni bil pripravljen prositi za manj. Dunya je ob robu Seama ugasnila glavni pogon in pustila le usmerjevalne potisnike, kajti ladja brez njih je hlod.

Vrh je prišel kakor dvigovanje tal sveta. Vratni okvir se ni raztrgal. Počasi se je razprl kakor dlan in Lark je na dolgem valu zdrsnila vanj, kakor da bi jo zid čakal, da jo prime. Pod palubo je Ysa začela brneti, tako nizko, da temu ni bilo mogoče reči pesem, zvok pa je prehajal iz trupa v trup, dokler niso pregrade z njim nežno zatrepetale.
Štiristo metrov je Lark nosilo.
Potem jo je val začel odnašati proti robu vratnega okvira.

**Dunya**  
Trideset metrov do zidu na levi strani. Potrebujem potisnike.

**Illuminara**  
Imaš še kaj drugega?

**Dunya**  
Ne.
Ničesar drugega ni bilo. Potisniki so se vžgali z drobnim brnenjem pri štiridesetih ciklih in val je prenehal biti dlan.

Ni je zdrobil. Vrgel jo je ven. Hrbtenica je počila z enim samim suhim zvokom, Illuminara pa je skočila na glavni nosilec in prevzela težo ladje. Držala jo je devetdeset sekund, medtem ko je posadka čez bok odhajala v rešilne čolne. Nato je Lark izpustila in ladja se je zložila sama vase kakor papir.
Enajst ljudi je imelo zlomljene kosti. Nihče ni umrl. Pristaniška ura je odštela še štirideset minut in Hale Corvane je stal pod njo s prekrižanimi rokami.

**Hale Corvane**  
Tri ure za rez, ki nas ni naučil ničesar. Štirideset minut za ladjo, ki te je naučila dveh stvari.

**Hale Corvane**  
Potem hočem preostanek odgovora. Ne prej.

**Dunya**  
Jaz sem vžgala potisnike.

**Illuminara**  
Imela si trideset metrov in ničesar drugega. Nikoli ti nisem povedala, v kaj boš zadela. To moram nositi jaz, ne ti.
V rešilnem čolnu je Ysa sedela z obvezanim zapestjem in še vedno brnela nikomur.

**Ysa**  
Nosilo nas je, medtem ko smo brneli.

**Illuminara**  
Res je. Nosilo nas je štiristo metrov, medtem ko smo bili mirni, in vrglo nas je ven v trenutku, ko smo vžgali motorje. To sta dve stvari, ki se ju moramo naučiti, ne ena: kdaj se ga dotakniti in kako mora dotik zveneti.

scenes.title: Ocean
paragraphs: *V Uluunu, skozi okno · sedemindvajset ur, mirna voda*
Najprej je določila pogoje, kajti obisk, ki ga ni mogoče končati, ni obisk.

**Illuminara**  
Če trzne, odidem. Ne takrat, ko ga bom razumela. Ko trzne. Nato ostanem zunaj večji del ure, da se odloči, in vrnem se le zato, da znova ponudim, nikoli da vprašam zakaj.

**Dunya**  
Trije udarci po tvoji roki in tvoje ime. Če v četrt ure ne boš odgovorila, pridem noter s kladivom.
Okno je odprla za širino dlani in njegova vrata pustila tam, kjer so jo lahko našli Dunyini trije udarci. Njeno telo je ostalo na pristaniški palubi. Preostanek nje se je spustil v težo.

Ni bila voda in ni bila tema. Bil je pritisk, ogromen in počasen, um, ki ni govoril, temveč se je nagibal, nekaj prostranega, kar se je dvignilo na površje, vase sprejelo vrata in jih obdržalo. Ob mirni vodi je ves ocean bolel okoli ene same hladne črte, skozenj je kakor nit skozi tkanino teklo brnenje pri štiridesetih ciklih, ob črti pa so bile tri zaplate niča, kjer je nehal slišati. Ni segla po njih. Niso bile njene, da jih odpre. Občutila je eno željo, ki je ni imela pravice izpolniti s silo: da bi se ga dotaknilo nekaj, kar ne bi ničesar odvzelo.

Ocean je ob njenem prihodu trznil. Ni se prepirala. V istem dihu se je umaknila, nazaj na palubo in k Dunyinim trem udarcem, ter petdeset minut sedela z odprtimi dlanmi na kolenih. Prvi ne je bil odgovor in pustila ga je veljati kot takega.

Druga ponudba se je začela, ko se je val obrnil proti vrhu. Vstopila je manjša kot prej in prinesla le Ysino brnenje, enkrat, preden bi ga nosil kakršenkoli trup. Petindvajset ciklov, precej pod štiridesetimi cikli rezalnikov. Nizko, brez naglice, brez česarkoli pod njim.

Ocean ni trznil. Nagnil se je, ne proti njej, temveč proti brnenju. Ko je pustila, da je brnenje zamrlo, je nagib popustil in ves val je začel drseti proti svojemu robu, kakor voda teče proti robu nagnjenega pladnja. Želel je sredino, pa je nič ni označevalo. Zato je zastavila edino vprašanje, ki ga je imela. Brnenje je postavila nizko in na eno stran, in nagib je šel tja. Postavila ga je na sredino razpona, in nagib je šel tja. Kjer je bilo brnenje, tja je šel val.

Takrat je razumela Lark. Ysino brnenje je potovalo v tistem, kar je bilo nošeno, in ko je trup zaneslo, je z njim zaneslo tudi sredino. Brnenje pred trupi, na središčnici, bi bilo sredina, ki se ne premika. Bilo je držalo in zid ga je lahko vsak trenutek izpustil.
Val, ki se je vzpenjal proti vrhu, se je na poti za nekaj sekund zadržal.
*Morda,* je pomislila. *Ne obljuba. Ni mi dolžan obljube.*
Večino svojega življenja je bila največja stvar v večini prostorov. Tukaj stvar, ki jo je držala, ni imela razloga, da bi jo. Občutek je bil, kakor da ji je dovoljeno.
Trije udarci. Nato njeno ime. Vrnila se je.

scenes.title: Temna mesta
paragraphs: *Dvorana sveta, Harbor Nine · petindvajset ur*

Razložila je v štirih minutah. Ostali so trije vrhovi. Mesta bodo prečkala v treh valovih, z ugasnjenimi motorji in lučmi, vsak trup bo brnel, sledila pa bodo čolnu z ugasnjenim motorjem, usmerjevalcu, ki bo plul spredaj po središčnici in brnel pri Ysinih petindvajsetih ciklih. Uluun lahko ustavi katerikoli val tako, da zadrži svoje valovanje, in nihče ne bo vžgal pogona.

**Hale Corvane**  
Šest milijard ljudi na valu, ki smo mu nadeli držalo, v temi, na milost bitja, ki je včeraj vrglo ladjo čez pristanišče. Tudi Lark je brnela, Illuminara. V čem je tvoj čoln drugačen?

**Illuminara**  
Lark je svoje brnenje nosila v sebi, zato je šlo tja, kamor jo je zaneslo. Brnenje usmerjevalca gre pred nami, po središčnici, zato ima val sredino, ki se ne premika.

**Hale Corvane**  
In če se ustavi?

**Illuminara**  
Potem počakaš.

**Hale Corvane**  
In če se med čakanjem izteče čas?

**Illuminara**  
Potem nekateri od nas ne pridejo ven. Ne bom jih kupila z drugo harpuno, delegat.

**Hale Corvane**  
Potem odločitev ni tvoja. Ko se ustavi, pilot na vodilni palubi odloči, kdaj čakamo in kdaj stečemo proti čolnom. Ne bom dovolil, da oseba, ki bi lahko dvignila mesto, odloča, ali ga sme izpustiti. Dunya.

**Illuminara**  
Dogovorjeno. Odločitev je Dunyina in spoštovala jo bom.
Pristaniški delavec v zadnji vrsti je vstal z otroško rokavico, zloženo v pesti. Ime mu je bilo Marro Tell.

**Marro Tell**  
Ni mi všeč in ni mi všeč, da nihče ni vprašal nas, ki bomo sedeli v temi z otroki. Jaz imam tri. Ne bom brnel zidu.

**Illuminara**  
Ni ti treba. Obstaja druga pot, plovba po robu: čolni ob robu zidu na prvem vrhu, brez brnenja, trideset ur do oddaljene obale, medtem ko mesta prečkajo v šestih urah. Nocoj jo bom začrtala s pilotom po tvoji izbiri in nihče je ne bo imenoval pot strahopetcev.

**Marro Tell**  
Tako ji bodo rekli.

**Dunya**  
Potem mi bodo to povedali v obraz. Jaz bom odločala in z vodilne palube bom videla tvoje čolne.
Corvane je še vedno gledal zemljevid. To, kar je vprašal nato, ga je nekaj stalo.

**Hale Corvane**  
Tamsin Deep gre v zadnjem valu. Če se bo na kom ustavil, naj se ustavi na mojih štirih milijonih, potem ko bodo videli prva dva vala priti skozi.

**Illuminara**  
To je najtežje mesto v vrsti. Zakaj ga izbereš?

**Hale Corvane**  
Ker bi bil raje zadnji, ki ti verjame, kot prvi, ki se moti.

scenes.title: Prvi val
paragraphs: *Seam, paluba Veyra Hold, ugasnjene luči · triindvajset ur*

Ob vrhu se je vratni okvir odprl kakor za Lark in vanj je z ugasnjenimi motorji vstopilo sto triintrideset mest. Usmerjevalec je plul spredaj po središčnici, šest pilotov v mrtvem čolnu je brnelo pri Ysinih petindvajsetih ciklih. Illuminara je stala na vodilni palubi v svojem običajnem telesu, ob njej Ysin stol, Dunya pa pri ograji. V minuti je brnenje postalo dve milijardi ljudi z dlanmi na pregradah.
Val jih je dvignil kakor dih. V osmi minuti jih je začelo odnašati proti levemu robu. Usmerjevalca je zaneslo za dolžino trupa s črte in val je šel z njim.

**Dunya**  
Usmerjevalec, nazaj na sredino. Vsi drugi obdržite dlani spuščene.

Dunya ni segla po potisniku. Piloti čolna so premaknili svoj ton in val se je vrnil k njim, kakor se speči obrne proti toplemu hrbtu. Daleč na levi je ob robu v tišini na istem vrhu plula vrsta drobnih luči. Čolni Marra Tella. Nihče na njih ni brnel.
V enaintrideseti minuti se je val ustavil.

Ni jih stisnil. Ni jih vrgel. Ves val je preprosto obstal, sto triintrideset mest je viselo v živem tkivu, nikjer pa ni bilo nobenega zvoka razen brnenja. Nekje globoko v njegovem telesu je star rez zdrsnil pod plimo in se prebudil. Po odprtem kanalu se je s temne palube Tamsin Deep oglasil Hale Corvane.

**Hale Corvane**  
Veyra Hold, luči pravijo, da se je ustavil. Odločitev je tvoja, pilotka.

**Dunya**  
Lahko bi vžgali pogone. Ostalo je devet minut vrha.

**Ysa**  
Povej, zakaj ne. Hočem slišati na glas.

**Illuminara**  
Ker je edina stvar v tem celotnem prečkanju, ki sme reči ustavi. Če tega ne more, nas ni nikoli nosila. Razbili smo vrata z lepšimi manirami.

**Dunya**  
Potem ukazujem čakanje. Usmerjevalec, nadaljuj brnenje. Vsi drugi, dlani dol.

To je bilo najtežje, kar je Illuminara tisti dan storila, videti pa je bilo kakor nič. Stala je na temni palubi z močjo, ki bi lahko mesto dvignila na hrbet, pa je ni uporabila, in pilotka, ki je imela odločitev, je namesto nje ukazala čakanje.
Enajst minut se val ni premaknil. Nato se je premaknil, vrh, ki bi moral izginiti v štirideseti minuti, pa je ostal. Zadržal se je skoraj eno uro. Kit je vračal čas, ki ga je vzel.
Drugi val se je ustavil za štiri minute in nihče se ni dotaknil pogona. Tretji, s Tamsin Deep na čelu, se sploh ni ustavil.

scenes.title: Kar je nosil val
paragraphs: *Druga stran, nova tema · trideset ur po prvem valu*

Zvezd ni bilo. Šest milijard ljudi je stalo na palubah štiristo mest in gledalo nazaj proti kraju, kjer je bilo njihovo nebo. Calyx je ugasnil pred več urami, kakor ugasne hiša, ko se za njo zaprejo vrata.
Ysa je sedela na klopi z zapestjem v opornici. Čolni ob robu so prispeli v trideseti uri, prav vsi, in Marro Tell je po mostičku prišel s svojimi tremi otroki ter ni bil videti zadovoljen.

**Marro Tell**  
O temi nimam povedati ničesar prijaznega. Toda moji so živi in nihče ni brnel nikomur, ki tega ni želel. Naslednjič najprej vprašajte nas.

**Illuminara**  
Prav imaš. Najprej smo začrtali mesta in šele nato čolne. Naslednji načrt se začne pri tebi.

Za mesti je ležala Uluunova brazgotina, štirideset kilometrov dolg greben, bled in živ. Dunya je prišla po palubi s seznamom deset tisoč prostovoljcev za ekipe na brazgotini; Corvaneovo ime je bilo prvo.

**Dunya**  
Hodili bomo z njim. Ne naselili se. Hodili. Več generacij.

**Ysa**  
In brez zvezd.

**Illuminara**  
Brez zvezd. Toda nosil vas je in pustil, da brazgotina ostane odprta, da jo bomo lahko negovali.
Na zunanji strani so tri praznine še vedno ostajale brez odmeva. Ysa jih je dolgo gledala in ni rekla ničesar, Illuminara pa jim je pustila biti to, kar so bile.

Val se je obrnil. Uluun je odhajal, stran od zapirajoče se teme, proti poti, ki jo je izbral le on, mesta pa so bila nanizana za njim. Ko je valovanje prešlo pod vsakim od njih, je nekdo na krovu prižgal eno samo svetilko v njegovem ritmu. Ena in nato druga, pozdrav, ki je potoval počasi.

**Ysa**  
Ne odgovarja.

**Illuminara**  
Ni nam dolžan odgovora.

**Ysa**  
Zakaj potem upočasnjuje?
In res je, za las, ravno dovolj, da so ga luči na koncu vrste dohitele.

translation_sl.critic_line: Illuminara spozna, da ranjeni živi zid trzne še pred rezilom, ponudi mu zavrnljivo brnenje, odločitev preda pilotki, ki lahko ukaže čakanje, in šest milijard ljudi prečka sesedajoči se kozmos za čolnom z ugasnjenim motorjem, medtem ko zid ohrani svojo brazgotino in lastno pot.
